Mr. Bumble. The pompous, self-important workhouse master in Oliver Twist whose bloated dignity and misapplied authority over the poor reveal the cruelty embedded in institutional bureaucracy. He serves as the master of the workhouse where Oliver Twist is born and raised, presiding with corpulent self-satisfaction over starving children. He demonstrates the casual cruelty of the system through his own indifference and pomposity, speaking in elaborate phrases to obscure rather than illuminate. He participates in the decision to offer a reward for Oliver's capture after the boy flees, treating his young charge as an escaped criminal. Later, he marries the matron and becomes sexton, acquiring additional petty authority which he wields with the same unthinking arrogance. Public perception captures his ridiculous relationship to the justice system in the phrase attributed to his circle: "the law is a ass, a idiot." He represents Dickens' attack on the New Poor Law and the officials who administered it without compassion or wisdom. A man of affected speech and inflated ego, he personifies the petty tyrant satisfied with minor power over the helpless.
